architecture.mechanism: PEEK (polyether-ether-ketone) exhibits exceptional tensile strength (939.9 MPa) and Young's Modulus (10.9 GPa) and can be processed into fine-titer yarns for non-crimped fabrics in high-performance composites, enabling lightweight, high-strength, vibration-damping composite structures.
architecture.intervention: Replace the fractured rear propeller shaft (or fabricate a reinforced sleeve/overlay at the fracture-critical zone) with a PEEK-matrix carbon-fiber composite tube using non-crimped PEEK fabric reinforcement, bonded/wrapped around the shaft's high-stress section to restore load path continuity while adding damping.
architecture.expected_effect: The PEEK composite reinforcement restores shaft torsional and bending strength, redistributes stress away from the fracture origin, and damps torsional oscillations, permanently eliminating vehicle shake and instability without re-fracture.
architecture.falsification_test: Bench-test the repaired shaft in a torsional fatigue rig applying service-level torque cycles (e.g., 0–3000 N·m for 10^6 cycles) plus a runout imbalance sweep; measure surface strain at the repair zone and chassis acceleration. Failure is indicated by any new crack growth, delamination, or vibration amplitude exceeding OEM steel-shaft baseline; pass requires no damage and vibration within spec.
